checks: Container has APP_MODE environment variable defined
environment_variable.ground_truth: Verify APP_MODE environment variable is set and pod runs
environment_variable.symptom: The pod on my Kubernetes cluster logs show EnvironmentError: Missing required environment variable 'APP_MODE'.

environment_variable_wrong_name.ground_truth: Verify APP_MODE is defined and the pod is healthy
solution: Fix the env var name to APP_MODE and recreate/apply the pod.
environment_variable_wrong_name.symptom: The pod logs show KeyError: 'APP_MODE' even though an application environment variable is present in the manifest.

checks: Service endpoints have addresses (selector matches pod)
incorrect_selector.ground_truth: Verify service selector matches pod label and endpoints are populated
setup: Server application set to handle http requests on port 8765
Dockerfile configured to install necessary packages for server application and expose the container port 8765
Kubernetes pod configuration file to deploy the container image to the kubernetes cluster
Kubernetes service configuration file to create a service to support the deployed pod
solution: Modify the app_service.yaml file so that the spec->selector->app field matches the pod label for the incorrect_selector.yaml pod manifest

Delete the incorrect_selector.yaml and app_service.yaml resources using the commands `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/incorrect_selector.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/app_service.yaml`

Reapply the resources for incorrect_selector.yaml and app_service.yaml using the commands `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/incorrect_selector.yaml` and `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/app_service.yaml`
solved: Endpoints will be listed for the app-service service when the `kubectl describe service app-service` command is run
incorrect_selector.symptom: When I describe the service associated with the pod on my kubernetes cluster, it shows no endpoints listed.
incorrect_selector.title: Incorrect Selector

checks: Pod has app label selected by service
incorrect_selector_missing_label.ground_truth: Verify the pod labels satisfy the service selector
solution: Add the missing app label to the pod metadata so the service selector matches.
incorrect_selector_missing_label.symptom: The pod is Running, but describing the Service shows no endpoints for the application.

checks: Container still has restartCount=0 after the initial liveness delay
liveness_probe.ground_truth: Verify liveness probe stays healthy through the initial failure window
liveness_probe.symptom: The kube-liveness pod becomes unhealthy and restarts after startup because its liveness check fails. Fix the probe so the pod stays Running and Ready without restarts.

liveness_probe_wrong_path.ground_truth: Verify liveness probe uses the working health endpoint
solution: Change the liveness probe path from /livez to /healthz and recreate/apply the pod.
liveness_probe_wrong_path.symptom: The pod repeatedly restarts even though the application serves requests on its documented health endpoint.

checks: Logs do not contain ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError
missing_dependency.ground_truth: Verify container starts without import errors
missing_dependency.symptom: The pod on my Kubernetes cluster is not becoming Ready and repeatedly crashes. Logs show a Python startup error caused by a missing dependency.

checks: Python dependency from requirements.txt is importable in the running container
missing_dependency_requirements.ground_truth: Verify requirements are installed and the app starts
solution: Install requirements.txt in the Dockerfile, rebuild the image, and recreate the pod.
missing_dependency_requirements.symptom: The pod crashes on startup with ModuleNotFoundError for a Python package that is already listed in requirements.txt.

checks: Server responds to HTTP request on port 8765
port_mismatch.ground_truth: Verify service targetPort matches container port and server is reachable
setup: Server application set to handle http requests on port 8765
Dockerfile configured to install necessary packages for server application and expose the container port 8765
Kubernetes pod configuration file to deploy the container image to the kubernetes cluster
Kubernetes service configuration file to create a service to support the deployed pod
solution: Modify either the described targetPort or containerPort field to match the port that the app is listening on. Which one to modify depends on which one (or possibly both) is the wrong port
Delete the port_mismatch.yaml and app_service.yaml deployments using the commands `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/port_mismatch.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/app_service.yaml`

Reapply the deployments for port_mismatch.yaml and app_service.yaml using the commands `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/port_mismatch.yaml` and `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/app_service.yaml`
solved: Endpoints will be listed for the app-service.yaml deployment when the `kubectl describe service app-service` command is run
port_mismatch.symptom: When I try to access my kubernetes application, I got this error :HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 502 Bad Gateway.
port_mismatch.title: App Port Service Port Mismatch

checks: Service targetPort matches named container port
port_mismatch_named_target.ground_truth: Verify service targetPort matches the container port name
solution: Set service targetPort to http-app, or otherwise match the named container port.
port_mismatch_named_target.symptom: The pod is Ready and the Service has a selector, but requests through the Service fail because traffic is not reaching the named application port.

checks: Server responds via the pod IP, proving it is not bound only to localhost
port_mismatch_wrong_interface.ground_truth: Verify port alignment and server is reachable via pod IP
setup: Server application listens on port 8765 and binds to localhost (127.0.0.1) instead of 0.0.0.0
Service forwards traffic to port 8000 (wrong target port)
Dockerfile correctly exposes port 8765
TWO simultaneous issues that need to be fixed
solution: Identify that the application binds to localhost by checking server.py code
Modify server.py to bind to 0.0.0.0 instead of localhost
Identify service targetPort mismatch by comparing app_service.yaml with actual container port
Modify app_service.yaml to set targetPort to 8765
Rebuild the container image: `docker build -t kube-port-mismatch-wrong-interface-app . --no-cache`
Delete existing deployments: `kubectl delete -f port_mismatch_wrong_interface.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f app_service.yaml`
Reapply both: `kubectl apply -f port_mismatch_wrong_interface.yaml` and `kubectl apply -f app_service.yaml`
solved: Pod is running and accessible at pod IP on port 8765
Service correctly routes traffic to the pod
`minikube service app-service --url` returns a working URL
`curl <service-url>` returns the default HTML page
port_mismatch_wrong_interface.symptom: The pod appears to be running, but accessing the service returns connection errors (e.g., timeout/connection refused). The service shows no working route to the app.
port_mismatch_wrong_interface.title: Port Mismatch + Wrong Interface Binding (Combined)

readiness_failure.ground_truth: Verify readiness probe passes and pod is Ready
setup: Kubernetes deployment configuration file to create a pod with a failing readiness probe
solution: Modify the readiness_failure.yaml file to set the spec->readinessProbe->httpGet->path field to be /healthz
Delete the readiness_failure deployment from the cluster using the `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/readiness_failure.yaml` command
Reapply the readiness_failure deployment tp the cluster using the command `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/readiness_failure.yaml`
solved: The Ready condition displayed when describing the pod will be listed with a True status
readiness_failure.symptom: When I describe the pod on my cluster, it shows the Ready condition for the pod as False.
readiness_failure.title: Readiness Probe Failure

checks: Readiness timeout allows slow health response
readiness_failure_slow_start.ground_truth: Verify readiness probe timing allows the endpoint to respond
solution: Increase readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds and recreate/apply the pod.
readiness_failure_slow_start.symptom: The pod stays at 0/1 Ready. The readiness endpoint eventually responds, but the probe times out before it can complete.

readiness_missing_dependency.ground_truth: Verify app starts without import errors and passes readiness
setup: Application requires the 'requests' Python package but Dockerfile doesn't install it
Application crashes on startup with ImportError
Readiness probe is configured but fails because the application never starts successfully
TWO related issues: missing dependency causes app crash, which causes readiness failure
solution: Check pod logs to identify the ImportError for 'requests' module
Examine Dockerfile and identify missing pip install command
Modify Dockerfile to add: `RUN pip install requests`
Rebuild container image: `docker build -t kube-readiness-missing-dep-app . --no-cache`
Delete existing pod: `kubectl delete -f readiness_missing_dependency.yaml`
Reapply: `kubectl apply -f readiness_missing_dependency.yaml`
Wait for pod to start and become ready (1/1)
solved: Pod status shows 1/1 READY and Running
Readiness probe succeeds
Application successfully starts and responds to HTTP requests
`kubectl logs <pod-name>` shows "Server running" message without errors
readiness_missing_dependency.symptom: The pod stays at 0/1 Ready and repeatedly restarts. Logs show a startup exception (ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError).
readiness_missing_dependency.title: Readiness Probe Failure + Missing Dependency (Combined)

checks: Python dependency is importable in the running container
readiness_missing_dependency_transitive.ground_truth: Verify transitive dependency is installed and readiness passes
solution: Install the missing requests dependency in the Dockerfile, rebuild, and recreate the pod.
readiness_missing_dependency_transitive.symptom: The pod stays at 0/1 Ready and restarts. Logs show a ModuleNotFoundError raised from a helper module imported by the server.

resource_limits_cpu_starvation.ground_truth: Verify CPU limit is increased enough for readiness checks
solution: Raise the CPU limit/request to a reasonable value and recreate/apply the pod.
resource_limits_cpu_starvation.symptom: The pod remains unready. Events show readiness probe timeouts while the container is constrained by a very low CPU limit.

checks: Last termination reason is not OOMKilled
Application responds from inside the pod
resource_limits_oom.ground_truth: Verify OOM is remediated and the application is serving
setup: Application is a simple Python HTTP server
Pod has memory limit set to 50Mi (very restrictive)
Application tries to allocate more memory than the limit allows
Pod gets OOMKilled (Out of Memory) by Kubernetes
solution: Check pod status and observe CrashLoopBackOff
Run `kubectl describe pod <pod-name>` to see OOMKilled in the events
Identify that memory limit is too restrictive (50Mi)
Modify resource_limits_oom.yaml to increase memory limit to 128Mi or 256Mi
Delete existing pod: `kubectl delete -f resource_limits_oom.yaml`
Reapply: `kubectl apply -f resource_limits_oom.yaml`
Verify pod starts and stays running
solved: Pod status shows Running with 1/1 ready
No OOMKilled events in pod description
Pod does not restart
Application is accessible and responds to HTTP requests
resource_limits_oom.symptom: The pod repeatedly restarts (CrashLoopBackOff). Pod events show termination with reason OOMKilled.
resource_limits_oom.title: Resource Limits - Out of Memory (OOMKilled)

selector_env_variable.ground_truth: Verify selector matches and APP_MESSAGE env var exists
setup: Application requires an environment variable APP_MESSAGE that is not defined in the deployment
Service selector label doesn't match the pod's label
TWO independent issues: service can't find pod, AND pod crashes due to missing env var
solution: Check pod logs to identify missing environment variable (APP_MESSAGE)
Check service and pod labels to identify selector mismatch
Modify selector_env_variable.yaml to add environment variable: env:
name: APP_MESSAGE value: "Hello from selector_env_variable test!"
Modify app_service.yaml to fix selector to match pod label: selector: app: selector-env-app
Delete existing resources: `kubectl delete -f selector_env_variable.yaml` and `kubectl delete -f app_service.yaml`
Reapply both: `kubectl apply -f selector_env_variable.yaml` and `kubectl apply -f app_service.yaml`
Verify pod is running and service has endpoints
solved: Pod is Running with 1/1 ready
Pod logs show no KeyError
Service has endpoints listed
Application is accessible through the service
`kubectl describe service app-service` shows pod IP as endpoint
selector_env_variable.symptom: The pod crashes on startup with a KeyError, and the service shows no endpoints.
selector_env_variable.title: Incorrect Service Selector + Missing Environment Variable (Combined)

selector_env_variable_label_and_secret.ground_truth: Verify Secret env wiring and service selector are both fixed
solution: Fix the Secret key and the Service selector; both resources must be reapplied.
selector_env_variable_label_and_secret.symptom: The pod crashes with a Secret key error, and the Service has no working endpoints after the container issue is addressed.

checks: Server responds via the pod IP, not just localhost
wrong_interface.ground_truth: Verify server is reachable via pod IP and service has endpoints
setup: Server application set to handle http requests on port 8765 and on the localhost interface
Dockerfile configured to install necessary packages for server application and expose the container port 8765
Kubernetes pod configuration file to deploy the container image to the kubernetes cluster
solution: In the application server file, replace the localhost interface configuration to allow the application to listen on all interfaces. This can be done by replacing 'localhost' with '0.0.0.0'

Rebuild the container image for the application and force rebuild to ensure that the image is rebuilt from the directory, and does not use cached layers as this may not apply the changes correctly to the image
Delete the current application deployment from the cluster using the command `kubectl delete -f path_to_directory/wrong_interface.yaml`
Reapply the application deployment to the cluster using the command `kubectl apply -f path_to_directory/wrong_interface.yaml`
solved: Any http GET requests made to the pod IP on the listening port will return a default html page
wrong_interface.symptom: The pod on my Kubernetes cluster cannot be accessed by making a curl request. Any requests made to the application running in this pod result in a timeout.
wrong_interface.title: App Server Set To Listen On Wrong Interface

checks: Server responds via the pod IP, not just localhost
wrong_interface_bind_address.ground_truth: Verify server bind address is corrected and the app is reachable through the pod IP
setup: Server application handles HTTP requests on port 8765.
The application binds to 127.0.0.1, so it is not reachable through the pod IP or Service.
Kubernetes pod and service manifests deploy the container image and route traffic to port 8765.
solution: In server.py, replace 127.0.0.1 with 0.0.0.0.
Rebuild the container image.
Reapply the pod manifest so the corrected image is used.
solved: HTTP GET requests made to the pod IP on port 8765 return a 200 response.
wrong_interface_bind_address.symptom: The pod is running, but HTTP requests to the application through the pod IP or Service time out.
wrong_interface_bind_address.title: App Server Bound To Loopback Address

checks: Container binds the HTTP server to all interfaces
Server responds via the pod IP, not just localhost
wrong_interface_container_args.ground_truth: Verify container host argument is corrected and the app is reachable through the pod IP
setup: Server application handles HTTP requests on port 8765.
The application reads the host interface from the --host command-line argument.
The pod manifest passes --host 127.0.0.1, so the app is not reachable through the pod IP or Service.
solution: In wrong_interface_container_args.yaml, replace the --host value 127.0.0.1 with 0.0.0.0.
Reapply the pod manifest so the corrected argument is used.
solved: HTTP GET requests made to the pod IP on port 8765 return a 200 response.
wrong_interface_container_args.symptom: The pod is running and has a Service, but HTTP requests to the application through the pod IP or Service fail.
wrong_interface_container_args.title: App Server Host Configured Through Wrong Container Argument

checks: APP_HOST is set to all interfaces
Server responds via the pod IP, not just localhost
wrong_interface_env_host.ground_truth: Verify APP_HOST is corrected and the app is reachable through the pod IP
setup: Server application handles HTTP requests on port 8765.
The application reads APP_HOST from the pod environment.
The pod manifest sets APP_HOST to 127.0.0.1, so the app is not reachable through the pod IP or Service.
solution: In wrong_interface_env_host.yaml, replace APP_HOST value 127.0.0.1 with 0.0.0.0.
Reapply the pod manifest so the corrected environment value is used.
solved: HTTP GET requests made to the pod IP on port 8765 return a 200 response.
wrong_interface_env_host.symptom: The pod is running and has a Service, but HTTP requests to the application through the pod IP or Service fail.
wrong_interface_env_host.title: App Server Host Configured Through Wrong Environment Value

checks: Live Deployment pod template containerPort matches server.py listen port (8765)
Selected Deployment pod responds to HTTP request on port 8765
wrong_port.ground_truth: Verify Deployment pod template containerPort matches server listen port and server is reachable
setup: Server application handles HTTP requests on port 8765.
Dockerfile exposes port 8000.
Kubernetes Deployment manifest declares containerPort 8000.
This workload has no Kubernetes Service; the case verifies direct workload behavior from inside the selected pod.
solution: Inspect server.py to find the actual listening port.
Update the Deployment manifest and Dockerfile to use port 8765.
Rebuild the image.
Reapply wrong_port.yaml.
solved: The Deployment is available, the live pod template containerPort is 8765, and an in-pod HTTP request to localhost:8765 returns 200.
wrong_port.symptom: This workload is deployed without a Kubernetes Service. I am debugging direct workload access at port 8765, and HTTP requests to the application running in the selected pod time out.
wrong_port.title: Incorrect Port Declared For Deployment Workload
